audit.why: 50.54% over 1306 games and the level chart (Rumble 2/3/6, Wukong late) match the written story: Rumble owns short trades from level 2 until Stone Skin plus armour items shrink his burst. Nothing to change in the difficulty framing.

audit.whatIsWrong: All four spike entries describe Wukong's power curve by slot letter only — 'his W clone', 'his E-R engage', 'Wukong's armor stacking'. The packet flags this outright: the matchup never names a single Wukong ability.
audit.why: A player reading the loading screen needs the name to recognise the cast. 'Armor stacking' is Stone Skin, and it stacks while he fights, so it is a within-fight spike, not just an item spike — that changes when you commit.
audit.corrected: Name Stone Skin, Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone at their spikes, with the rank-1 cooldowns that make the spike actionable.
sources: packet defect: never names any of Wukong's abilities

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions that decide this lane are absent. First, Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset — the text warns about 'Q armor shred' but never that the wind-up is the tell. Second, Warrior Trickster makes Wukong Invisible while the clone stands where he was; the text says the clone 'absorbs' Electro-Harpoon but never that Wukong himself is unselectable during it, which is why the harpoon locks onto the wrong body.
audit.why: Riot's text for Crushing Blow: 'Wukong's next attack gains attack range, deals bonus damage, and reduces the target's armor.' That is a reset, and the extra range (250 to 350 by rank) means the wind-up happens further out than a normal auto. Warrior Trickster: 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone.' Electro-Harpoon is a projectile with no smart-targeting, so the clone is what it finds.
audit.corrected: State the auto reset as the step-back cue, name the Invisible portion of Warrior Trickster, and give its 22s rank-1 cooldown as the punish window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Q autoReset flag + description, W description)

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid-game section says 'never let Heat cap at 100 while he has E available' without saying how long E is down for, so there is no window to play into.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7 seconds. That is short enough that the advice is really 'assume it is up', and long enough at rank 1 that a burnt Nimbus Strike is a real Overheat-safe window. Cyclone at 130 seconds rank 1 is the number that makes a level-6 all-in refusal worth it.
audit.corrected: Give Nimbus Strike 10s at rank 1 and Cyclone 130s at rank 1 alongside the Heat advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike claims Wukong 'dives into a burning wall he cannot cancel'. Nothing in Riot's Cyclone description says the spin cannot be ended early, and the kit file's needsResearch block is empty, which means unknown, not no.
audit.why: Asserting an ability cannot be cancelled is exactly the kind of claim a player will trust and then die to. The safe and equally useful version is positional: Cyclone has a 315 radius and he must Nimbus Strike to a target first, so his landing spot is knowable.
audit.corrected: Drop the cancel claim and keep the placement advice — aim Equalizer at the Nimbus Strike landing spot.

edits.before: Your Q-into-double-Harpoon combo comes fully online — Wukong cannot walk through sustained Flamespitter without losing the trade badly.
edits.after: Q into double-Harpoon is online — but Crushing Blow is an auto reset, so its wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to leave his 350 range.

edits.before: Equalizer punishes his E-R engage path: drop it across his spin landing zone and he dives into a burning wall he cannot cancel.
edits.after: Equalizer punishes the Nimbus Strike into Cyclone engage: drop it where he lands, not on his head, and he spins inside your fire.

edits.before: Wukong's W clone absorbs your Electro-Harpoon slow and burns your cooldown — watch the tell before throwing E.
edits.after: Warrior Trickster turns him Invisible and the clone eats your Electro-Harpoon — 22s at rank 1, punish once spent.

edits.before: Wukong's armor stacking and Sterak's Gage absorb your frontloaded magic burst; his R knockup chains more reliably once your burst window shrinks.
edits.after: Stone Skin stacks armour and health regen the longer he fights, so your frontloaded burst shrinks and Cyclone's knockup chains more reliably.

edits.before: Pre-aim Equalizer across his R landing zone to punish the spin with a burning wall he walks into
edits.after: Pre-aim Equalizer where Nimbus Strike drops him so Cyclone spins inside your fire rather than through it

edits.before: Use W clone to eat your Electro-Harpoon and waste the slow before the real body commits to an E-Q trade
edits.after: Use Warrior Trickster to go Invisible and leave a clone that eats your Electro-Harpoon before Nimbus Strike lands

edits.before: Wukong's Q armor shred rewards extended auto trades at Level 1 — anchor to Flamespitter range and don't brawl.
edits.after: Crushing Blow shreds armour and resets his auto on 8s at rank 1 — anchor to Flamespitter range and never brawl autos.

edits.before: At Level 1 you are not the aggressor yet — Wukong's Q armor shred means early extended autos go his way, so anchor your trade pattern to Flamespitter: step up, let Q tick, back off before he can Q-shred and auto back. Level 2 flips it: your Q-into-Harpoon slow punishes every step he takes toward you, and he has no reliable way to close through sustained cone damage without eating the empowered slow on top. By Level 3 you are the clear favorite in any short trade — stack Heat into the Danger Zone and chain Q into double-E, forcing him off the wave. The one thing that ends you early is the W clone: he will throw his body forward, you will instinctively throw Harpoon at the closest target, and the clone eats the slow while the real Wukong walks up free. Watch for the W animation flicker before you throw E.
edits.after: At Level 1 you are not the aggressor — Crushing Blow reduces your armour and resets his auto, so extended autos go his way. Anchor to Flamespitter: step up, let Q tick, back off on the Crushing Blow wind-up rather than after it lands. Level 2 flips it: your Q-into-Harpoon slow punishes every step he takes toward you, and Nimbus Strike is his only clean way through sustained cone damage. By Level 3 you are the clear favorite in any short trade — stack Heat into the Danger Zone and chain Q into double-E, forcing him off the wave. The one thing that ends you early is Warrior Trickster: he goes Invisible and dashes away, leaving a clone your Harpoon locks onto while the real Wukong walks up free. It is 22 seconds at rank 1, so the moment he spends it the lane is yours again.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the tightest stretch of the lane — Wukong is building toward a first armor item and his raw dueling closes the gap on your sustained damage, so the Danger Zone management has to be clean or trades go neutral instead of your way. Never let Heat cap at 100 while he has E available; the Overheat silence window is exactly when he dashes in and chains his full combo without you being able to react with W. Level 6 reopens your edge in a completely different direction: the moment you have Equalizer, his R becomes telegraphed. His spin is a tight radius and a predictable landing spot — drop Equalizer across the path he is committing to and he spins directly into the burning wall. You do not need to hit the initial rocket line; just place it so the fire carpet is where he lands.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the tightest stretch of the lane — Wukong is building toward a first armor item and Stone Skin stacks more resistances the longer any single fight runs, so the Danger Zone management has to be clean or trades go neutral instead of your way. Never let Heat cap at 100 while Nimbus Strike is up: it is only 10 seconds at rank 1, and the Overheat silence window is exactly when he dashes in and chains his full combo without you being able to react with W. Level 6 reopens your edge in a completely different direction. Cyclone is 130 seconds at rank 1 and its radius is tight, and he has to Nimbus Strike onto you before he spins — which tells you exactly where he will be standing. Drop Equalizer on that landing spot rather than the line he travels. You do not need the initial rockets to hit; you need the fire carpet to be where he lands.

notes: The packet's stated defect (no Wukong ability is ever named) is real and every edit above is aimed at it. I deliberately removed the claim that Wukong 'cannot cancel' Cyclone — Riot's description does not say so and the kit's needsResearch is empty, which the brief defines as unknown. Rumble's kit file flags Scrap Shield (W) with 'knockup' and 'terrain'; Riot's description is shield plus move speed only, so I wrote nothing that has Scrap Shield stopping Nimbus Strike or Warrior Trickster. Item names already in the text (Sterak's Gage, Black Cleaver, Void Staff, Shadowflame, Luden's) were left alone — I could not verify the 26.15 item pool locally.
